s.d: six-legged winged insect characterized by the fact that its third pair of legs is elongated and adapted to hopping; Acrididae family; moves in swarms that migrate to new areas, which they colonize; at other times lives solitary or in small groups; eaten cooked by toasting, grilling, frying, or broiling, though in some places they are also eaten raw; because of their large numbers and swarming characteristics, locusts were a symbol of a vast attacking army against which there was no defense and also a symbol of divine punishment
s.c: The four NT contexts in which ἀκρίς occurs refer to these insects either as being edible (⟦Matthew 3:4|Matthew 3:4⟧; ⟦Mark 1:6|Mark 1:6⟧) or as being very destructive (⟦Revelation 9:3|Revelation 9:3⟧).|Some persons have assumed that the reference to grasshoppers being eaten by John the Baptist should be understood not as the insects but as carob pods, but there is neither linguistic nor cultural evidence to support such an interpretation.|In a number of parts of the world there are different kinds of grasshoppers/locusts, some of which are edible, and others which are not edible. It is therefore important in the contexts of ⟦Matthew 3:4|Matthew 3:4⟧ and ⟦Mark 1:6|Mark 1:6⟧ to select a term which designates edible insects.

s.d: a relatively large building normally used for legal hearings, though possibly also employed for more general purposes
s.c: In a number of languages ἀκροατήριον may be rendered as ‘a large hall’ or ‘a place where many people could gather together’ or ‘a building where many people could sit to listen.’

s.d: (derivative of ἀκροάομαι ‘to hear,’ not occurring in the NT) one who hears
s.c: In rendering ⟦Romans 2:13|Romans 2:13⟧, it may be necessary to specify certain limitations with regard to being ‘hearers,’ for example, ‘for not just those who listen to the Law are righteous in God’s sight’ or ‘for those who merely listen to the Law are not the ones who are righteous in God’s sight.’

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: a state of being uncircumcised by not having the foreskin of the penis cut off{N:001}
s.g: being uncircumcised; the foreskin not cut off

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: a collective for those who are uncircumcised
s.c: In translating ⟦Galatians 2:7|Galatians 2:7⟧ it is essential in some languages to avoid the impression that there are two gospels, one for the Jews and another for the Gentiles. One may, therefore, render ⟦Galatians 2:7|Galatians 2:7⟧ as ‘I had been entrusted with the good news to the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been for the circumcised’ or even ‘God had given me and Peter the task of preaching the good news; I to the Gentiles and Peter to the Jews.’

s.dp: Constructions › Parts and Areas of Buildings
s.d: the cornerstone or capstone of a building, essential to its construction (this term occurs in the NT only figuratively in reference to Christ)
s.c: Some scholars have assumed that ἀκρογωνιαῖος would refer to the capstone occurring at the high point of a peaked roof, but in the NT ἀκρογωνιαῖος would probably refer to the type of stone which would have been used in the Temple in Jerusalem, and therefore it is far more likely to understand ἀκρογωνιαῖος as a cornerstone rather than a capstone of a peaked roof. It would not have referred to the keystone of an arch. Since, however, in many societies the use of ‘cornerstone’ is not known and in others it may have an entirely different function, it may be more satisfactory to use an expression such as ‘the most important stone’ or ‘the very important stone.’ This serves to describe the function and significance of the cornerstone without trying to indicate precisely its location or form.

s.d: the best part of the booty, particularly that which is offered to deity
s.g: the best of the booty; the finest spoils; the most valuable plunder

s.d: the extreme limit of a space
the tip or top of a pointed object

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a friend of Paul and the husband of Priscilla
to refuse to recognize the force or power of something
s.g: to invalidate the authority of; to reject; to disregard
s.c: In both ⟦Matthew 15:6|Matthew 15:6⟧ and ⟦Mark 7:13|Mark 7:13⟧ the emphasis is upon the fact that people had regarded traditions as having greater authority than the word of God.

s.d: pertaining to not being prevented
pertaining to not being willing to do something
s.g: not willing; not of one’s own free will; not a matter of free choice
s.c: Expressions of ‘not being willing to do something’ may often be rendered as ‘being forced to do something’ or ‘doing something because one has to.’

s.d: a jar made of alabaster stone
s.c: An alabaster jar normally had a rather long neck which was broken off for the contents to be used. It served primarily as a container for precious substances such as perfumes.|In translating ‘alabaster jar’ many translators have simply used a term meaning ‘jar’ or ‘flask’ and have either employed a descriptive qualifier, for example, ‘made of alabaster stone’ or ‘made of valuable stone’ or ‘made of valuable stone called alabaster.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Arrogance, Haughtiness, Pride
s.d: a state of pride or arrogance, but with the implication of complete lack of basis for such an attitude
s.g: false arrogance; pretentious pride; boastful haughtiness
s.c: ‘Pretentious pride’ may be rendered as ‘constantly talking about how great oneself is.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Arrogance, Haughtiness, Pride
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀλαζονεία<SDBG:ἀλαζονεία:000000>} ‘pretentious pride,’ {D:88.219}) one who is pretentiously proud and given to bragging about it
s.c: In a number of languages an arrogant person is described figuratively as ‘one who speaks big words about himself’ or ‘one whose mouth is too big for his body.’

s.d: to make a loud, reverberating sound

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Laugh, Cry, Groan
s.d: to cry or weep intensely and with wailing
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ἀλαλάζω is a term or phrase referring to ritual or ceremonial weeping or wailing. This would not necessarily imply lack of sincerity, but it would be typical of what would frequently occur in many societies in the case of the type of presumed death reported in ⟦Mark 5:38|Mark 5:38⟧.

s.d: pertaining to what cannot be uttered or expressed{N:001}
s.g: what cannot be expressed in words

s.d: pertaining to not being able to speak or talk
s.g: dumb; mute; unable to speak; incapable of talking

s.dp: Activities Involving Liquids or Masses › Application and Removal of Liquids or Masses
s.d: to anoint with a liquid, normally oil or perfume

s.dp: Time › Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
s.d: the name of the third Roman watch during the night, called ‘cockcrow’ (see {L:φυλακή<SDBG:φυλακή:000002>}[c] ‘watch,’ {D:67.196})
s.g: before dawn; when the cock crows

s.d: male domestic fowl, dark brownish red, with orange-red neck hackles, a smallish red comb on the top of the head, and red lappets on each side under the beak; the hen is a lighter brownish red and has a smaller comb; significance in the Bible seems related to the fact that cocks crow very early in the morning, announcing the coming dawn

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of Ἀλεξανδρία ‘Alexandria,’ not occurring in the NT) a person who lives in or is a native of Alexandria

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of Ἀλεξανδρία ‘Alexandria,’ not occurring in the NT) pertaining to Alexandria

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the son of Simon of Cyrene

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a member of the high-priestly family

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a Jew of Ephesus

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a false teacher in the church{N:001}

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a coppersmith and opponent of Paul{N:001}
a powder made by grinding the wheat berry; used in baking, esp. bread
s.c: In some languages wheat flour is described as ‘ground wheat’ or ‘powdered wheat.’

s.d: the content of that which is true and thus in accordance with what actually happened
s.c: In ⟦John 8:32|John 8:32⟧ ἀλήθεια is used to refer to the revelation of God that Jesus brings or, perhaps, to Jesus himself for what he actually is as the revelation of God.

s.d: (idioms, literally: ‘in truth,’ ‘upon truth,’ and ‘according to truth’) pertaining to being a real or actual event or state{N:001}
to communicate what is true
s.g: to speak the truth; to tell the truth
s.c: In a number of languages it may be difficult to employ a highly abstract term such as ‘truth.’ Accordingly, one may find it necessary to relate ‘truth’ in ⟦Galatians 4:16|Galatians 4:16⟧ to the immediate context, for example, ‘… by telling you what they really want to do’ or ‘… what all this really means.’

s.d: pertaining to being in accordance with historical fact
s.c: In a number of languages ‘the truth’ may be rendered simply as ‘what really is’ or ‘what is so’ or ‘what has happened.’

s.d: pertaining to being real and not imaginary{N:001}
s.c: The figurative or symbolic sense of this statement does not, of course, take away from its reality.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Honesty, Sincerity
s.d: pertaining to being truthful and honest
s.g: truthful; honest; a person of integrity
s.c: In a number of languages one must translate ἀληθής in ⟦Matthew 22:16|Matthew 22:16⟧ as ‘you always say what is true.’

s.d: pertaining to being real and not imaginary{N:001}
s.c: In some languages ‘the only one who is really God’ can only be expressed as ‘the only God who exists’ or ‘who is God and there are no other gods.’

s.d: pertaining to being in accordance with historical fact
pertaining to being what something should be
to grind grain in a mill
s.c: In ⟦Luke 17:35|Luke 17:35⟧ and also in ⟦Matthew 24:41|Matthew 24:41⟧ the reference is evidently to a hand mill, which was normally operated by two women working together. In societies in which such mills are not known, translators have frequently substituted the process of pounding grain by means of a mortar and pestle.

s.d: pertaining to being real and not imaginary{N:001}
one whose occupation is to catch fish
to catch fish, whether by means of a line or by a net
(a causative derivative of {L:ἅλς<SDBG:ἅλς:000000>} ‘salt,’ {D:5.25}) to cause something to taste salty
s.g: to apply salt to something; to restore the flavor to salt
s.c: In ⟦Matthew 5:13|Matthew 5:13⟧ one may employ a causative such as ‘how will the salt be made salty again’ or ‘how can one cause the salt to return.’ In ⟦Mark 9:49|Mark 9:49⟧ the meaning is particularly obscure. According to OT requirements sacrifices were to be salted (⟦Leviticus 2:13|Leviticus 2:13⟧), and it may be that in ⟦Mark 9:49|Mark 9:49⟧ the fire is regarded as an equivalent of salt and as a symbol of suffering and sacrifice by which the disciple is tested.

s.d: that which has been ritually defiled
a marker of more emphatic contrast (as compared with {L:δέ<SDBG:δέ:000002>}[c], {D:89.124})
s.c: ἀλλά also occurs with μᾶλλον and ἤ in more emphatic phrases marking contrast: ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον δουλευέτωσαν ‘on the contrary, they are to serve (them) even better’ ⟦1 Timothy 6:2|1 Timothy 6:2⟧; οὐχί, λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀλλ᾽ ἢ διαμερισμόν ‘not (peace), I tell you, but rather division’ ⟦Luke 12:51|Luke 12:51⟧.

s.d: a marker of a series of coordinate relations which are contrastive with a previously identified event or state
a marker of transition, with a slightly adversative implication in some contexts, often best left untranslated
s.c: In ⟦Romans 15:21|Romans 15:21⟧ there is certainly no adversative value in the conjunction ἀλλά; if anything, it would only mark some underlying reason, but again it seems best to leave ἀλλά untranslated and to regard it simply as a transitional marker.

s.d: a marker of contrastive emphasis
a marker of sets of items in contrast with one another
s.g: on the one hand … but on the other hand

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Different Kind or Class
s.d: to cause a difference by altering the character or nature of something
s.g: to change; to alter; to make different

s.d: to exchange one thing for another{N:001}

s.dp: Spacial Extensions › Extension From a Source
s.d: extension from a source which is different
s.g: from elsewhere; from some other way

s.d: a position other than the one in the immediate context
to employ an analogy or likeness in communicating
s.g: to speak allegorically; to employ an analogy; to use a likeness

s.d: (a borrowing from Hebrew, literally: praise Yahweh) an expression of praise
a reciprocal reference between entities

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Political
s.d: a person belonging to a different socio-political group, with the implication of lack of kinship ties
to leap or to jump into the air

s.dp: Physical Events and States › Events Involving Liquids and Dry Masses
s.d: the action of water forming bubbles and welling up from underneath the ground
s.g: to bubble up; to well up
s.c: In the NT ἅλλομαι occurs only in the figurative context of ⟦John 4:14|John 4:14⟧.|In some languages expressions referring to the flowing of water from a spring depend upon the extent or continuity of such a flow. If the spring is a perennial one, that is to say, if it flows all the time, it may be designated by one term, while if it is intermittent, that is, flows only during the rainy season, it may be referred to by quite a different term. There may also be distinctions as to whether the water flows out and then down or whether it actually comes up from below the surface. In ⟦John 4:14|John 4:14⟧ the direction of flow is not important, but it is important to use a term which would indicate continuous flowing.

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Different Kind or Class
s.d: pertaining to that which is different in kind or class from all other entities{N:001}

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Different Kind or Class
s.d: pertaining to that which is other than some other item implied or identified in a context{N:001}

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Being a Busybody
s.d: one who busies himself in the affairs of others in an unwarranted manner

s.dp: Discourse Referentials › Whom or What Spoken or Written About
s.d: a reference to what belongs to someone else
s.g: belonging to another; belonging to someone else

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Political
s.d: a person from another geographical or cultural region and/or one not known to members of the socio-political group in question
s.c: In ⟦John 10:5|John 10:5⟧ the most satisfactory rendering of ‘stranger’ is often ‘someone who is not known,’ in other words, ‘they will not follow someone whom they do not know’ or ‘… recognize.’

s.d: pertaining to being opposed as a result of one’s being essentially different
s.g: to be strongly opposed to; to be an enemy of
s.c: Meanings involving enmity, hostility, and opposition are frequently idiomatic in nature and are derived primarily from four major experiential sources: (1) psychological attitudes, ‘to have one’s heart burn against’; (2) gestures, ‘to frown against’ or ‘to refuse to snap fingers’ (snapping fingers being a particular form of greeting in various parts of Africa); (3) body stance, ‘to stand against’; and (4) movement, ‘to turn one’s back against’ or ‘to turn away from.’

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: a person not belonging to the ethnic group in question (from the specifically Jewish point of view, one who is not a Jew, but a Gentile)

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Different Kind or Class
s.d: pertaining to that which is different in kind or class from all other entities{N:001}
to separate grain from the husks of plants, either by beating or by being tread on by farm animals
s.c: In a number of societies the idea of having animals tread out grain seems to be extremely wasteful and unsanitary, but there is no way of avoiding a translation of such passages in a more or less literal fashion; otherwise, there is no meaning to the context. It may also be important to provide some type of marginal note to explain more clearly what was involved.

s.d: pertaining to a lack of capacity to reason or think properly
s.g: without reason; not able to reason
s.c: In rendering ⟦2 Peter 2:12|2 Peter 2:12⟧ one may translate ‘creatures unable to reason’ as ‘wild animals,’ for this is clearly the reference of the phrase ἄλογα ζῷα.

s.d: pertaining to not providing a reason or cause, in view of something being contrary to reason
s.c: In some languages the equivalent of being unreasonable is being something which people should not think. Note that ἄλογος refers to that which is contrary to proper reasoning, while ἄλογος (LN 30.12) pertains to a lack of capacity to reason.

s.d: an aromatic resin of a lily-like plant, often used for embalming a corpse
s.c: As in the case of σμύρνα ‘myrrh’ (LN 6.208), translators normally borrow a term for ‘aloes’ and then employ some kind of marginal note to indicate the nature of the substance.

s.d: white crystalline substance, mainly consisting of sodium chloride, used for seasoning or preserving food
s.c: Since salt is a universal condiment, there is no difficulty involved in finding an adequate expression for it, but there is a difficulty in ⟦Matthew 5:13|Matthew 5:13⟧, since pure salt cannot lose its taste. In the ancient world, however, what was often sold as salt was highly adulterated and the sodium chloride could leach out in humid weather, in which case the residue (normally a form of lime) would be useless. It may, therefore, be important in some languages to provide a marginal note explaining the basis for the biblical statement concerning salt losing its flavor; otherwise, the parable may appear to be either meaningless or misleading.

s.d: (derivative of {L:ἅλς<SDBG:ἅλς:000000>} ‘salt,’ {D:5.25}) consisting of or pertaining to salt
s.c: It may be difficult in some languages to speak of ‘a salty spring’; rather, it may be necessary to say ‘a spring that produces water that tastes salty.’ In other instances one may have to say ‘a spring that flows from salty ground.’

s.d: pertaining to no longer experiencing sorrow or anxiety
s.g: relieved of anxiety; no longer sorrowful

s.dp: Artifacts › Instruments Used in Binding and Fastening
s.d: a series of connected metal links; used for binding objects together or restraining prisoners
s.c: In some languages a distinction is made between terms for a chain used in tying up a person and one employed in agricultural or industrial work.

s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἅλυσις<SDBG:ἅλυσις:000000>}[a] ‘chain,’ {D:6.16}) the state of being in prison
s.c: The state of being a prisoner is often expressed somewhat idiomatically, for example, ‘to be tied hand and foot,’ ‘to be chained like a dog,’ or ‘to look through iron bars.’

s.d: pertaining to being of no advantage
s.g: of no advantage; without special benefit

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the father of Ἰάκωβος[c]

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: the father of Λευί[a]
a surface of hard ground or stone where grain was threshed out, either by beating or having animals trample upon it
s.c: The meaning of ἅλων as ‘threshing floor’ forms the basis for the figurative extension of meaning (a metonymy) referring to the threshed grain still lying on the threshing floor (see LN 3.43). The meaning may be made clear by rendering ‘to thresh out completely all of the grain.’ On the other hand, it is possible to interpret ἅλων in ⟦Matthew 3:12|Matthew 3:12⟧ in a literal sense and translate ‘he will clean up his threshing floor,’ that is, by gathering up the grain and getting rid of the straw and chaff.

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἅλων<SDBG:ἅλων:000000>}[a] ‘threshing floor,’ {D:7.65}) grain in the process of being threshed
s.c: ἅλων in ⟦Matthew 3:12|Matthew 3:12⟧ may also be interpreted as a threshing floor (see LN 7.65).

s.d: animal looking like a longhaired dog with a pointed nose and a bushy tail; either reddish with white underparts (fox) or yellowish brown with red tips to the fur on the back (jackal); scavenger; associated with destruction and devastation, and also with being insignificant but self-important; also intelligent and quick-witted, crafty
s.c: Though the Greek term ἀλώπηξ and the corresponding Hebrew terms used in the OT may refer to either a fox or a jackal, ἀλώπηξ in the NT seems to refer primarily to a fox (see Fauna and Flora of the Bible, pp. 31-32, for certain significant distinctions between foxes and jackals).|In areas of the world where the fox is not known, one can sometimes speak of ‘a small wild dog’ or ‘an animal like a small wild dog.’ In other instances translators have borrowed the term ‘fox’ from a dominant language in the area and have then explained the appearance and habits of the animal in a glossary.|For ἀλώπηξ in a figurative sense as applied by Jesus to Herod Antipas, see LN 88.120.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Bad, Evil, Harmful, Damaging
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἀλώπηξ<SDBG:ἀλώπηξ:000000>}[a] ‘fox,’ {D:4.10}) a wicked person, probably with the implication of being cunning and treacherous
s.c: Some scholars, however, suggest that ἀλώπηξ in ⟦Luke 13:32|Luke 13:32⟧ may imply ‘worthlessness.’|Rendering ἀλώπηξ in ⟦Luke 13:32|Luke 13:32⟧ by a term meaning ‘fox’ may sometimes be misleading, since in some cultures the fox is regarded as a particularly wise animal, and therefore referring to a person as a fox may be a compliment. A local term for ‘fox’ may have other connotations which are quite undesirable. For example, in some languages a term for fox is used to designate a male or female prostitute, usually of the lowest grade.

s.d: the capture or catching of animals

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: a point of time which is emphatically simultaneous with another point of time
a marker of association, involving additional items affected by some event
pertaining to one who has not acquired a formal education, and hence with the implication of being stupid and ignorant{N:001}
pertaining to not losing the wonderful, pristine character of something
s.g: unfading; not losing brightness; retaining its wonderful character

s.d: pertaining to not losing the wonderful, pristine character of something
s.g: unfading; not losing brightness; retaining its wonderful character

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sin, Wrongdoing, Guilt
s.d: to act contrary to the will and law of God
s.g: to sin; to engage in wrongdoing; sin

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sin, Wrongdoing, Guilt
s.d: that which someone has done in violating the will and law of God

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sin, Wrongdoing, Guilt
s.d: to act contrary to the will and law of God
s.g: to sin; to engage in wrongdoing; sin

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Bad, Evil, Harmful, Damaging
s.d: a state of sinfulness as an integral element of someone’s nature
s.c: The implication of this statement made in criticism of Jesus in ⟦John 9:34|John 9:34⟧ was that he had not adhered rigorously to all the conventional requirements of the OT law as interpreted by the Pharisees.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sin, Wrongdoing, Guilt
s.d: the moral consequence of having sinned
s.c: A number of languages make a clear distinction between the active event of committing sin and the resulting moral effect of guilt, so that one must speak of ‘committing sin’ but ‘forgiving guilt.’ This is often required in some languages since a term meaning ‘to forgive’ is literally ‘to wipe away,’ ‘to erase,’ ‘to blot out,’ or ‘to return to someone.’ The actual event of sinning often does not fit with such verb expressions, since it is not the event itself which is eliminated but the moral consequences of such an event, namely, the guilt.

s.d: pertaining to not having a witness
s.c: In ⟦Acts 14:17|Acts 14:17⟧ it may be rather difficult to introduce what is essentially a double negative, implied by ‘not’ and ‘without.’ Accordingly, ⟦Acts 14:17|Acts 14:17⟧ may be rendered as ‘by the good things he does, everyone can know about him from experience.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sin, Wrongdoing, Guilt
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἁμαρτάνω<SDBG:ἁμαρτάνω:000000>} ‘to sin,’ {D:88.289}) pertaining to sinful behavior

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sin, Wrongdoing, Guilt
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἁμαρτάνω<SDBG:ἁμαρτάνω:000000>} ‘to sin,’ {D:88.289}) a person who customarily sins
s.c: In contexts such as ⟦Mark 2:17|Mark 2:17⟧, ⟦Matthew 9:10|Matthew 9:10⟧, ⟦Luke 15:2|Luke 15:2⟧, etc., ἁμαρτωλός may refer to persons who were irreligious in the sense of having no concern for observing the details of the Law. Such people were often treated as social outcasts.

s.d: pertaining to a lack of conflict and contention
to cut down grass or grain in a field
s.c: In biblical times mowing would have been done by means of a scythe or sickle, instruments with curved blades especially appropriate for cutting grass or standing grain.

s.dp: Natural Substances › Precious and Semiprecious Stones and Substances
s.d: amethyst; usually purple or violet in color (see {D:2.29})

s.dp: Think › To Think About, with the Implied Purpose of Responding Appropriately
s.d: to not think about, and thus not respond appropriately to
s.g: to neglect; to disregard; to pay no attention to

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sin, Wrongdoing, Guilt
s.d: pertaining to being without fault or blame

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sin, Wrongdoing, Guilt
s.d: pertaining to being without fault or blame

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Worry, Anxiety, Distress, Peace
s.d: pertaining to not being concerned or anxious
s.g: without worry; unworried; free from concern

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State
s.d: pertaining to that which does not change from one state to another
s.g: not changing; unchanging; never to change

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: pertaining to not being readily shaken in one’s opinions or beliefs
(derivative of {L:μεταμέλομαι<SDBG:μεταμέλομαι:000000>}[a] ‘to regret,’ {D:25.270}, with a negative prefix) pertaining to not feeling regret as the result of what one has done
s.g: not regretful; not feeling sorry about

s.dp: Behavior and Related States › Change Behavior
s.d: pertaining to not being repentant
s.g: unrepentant; not turning to God; refusing to turn to God
s.c: In a number of languages it is difficult to speak of ‘a hard and unrepentant heart.’ A more satisfactory equivalent of this expression in ⟦Romans 2:5|Romans 2:5⟧ may be ‘but you are stubborn and refuse to repent’ or ‘… refuse to turn to God.’

s.d: (an idiom, literally: into that which is not measured) a point on a scale going beyond what is expected
s.c: In a number of languages one can perhaps best render this statement in ⟦2 Corinthians 10:13|2 Corinthians 10:13⟧ as ‘we will not boast too much’ or ‘we will boast only so much.’

s.d: strong affirmation of what is declared
s.g: truly; indeed; it is true that

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: a person for whom there is no record of a female parent or who has never had a female parent or whose mother has died

(derivative of {L:μιαίνω<SDBG:μιαίνω:000001>}[b] ‘to defile,’ {D:53.34}, with the addition of the negative prefix ἀ) pertaining to not being ritually defiled, with implications of accompanying moral defilement

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person in the genealogy of Jesus; compare Ἀμιναδάμ ({S:04200303300004}, apparatus)

s.dp: Natural Substances › Earth, Mud, Sand, Rock
s.c: ἄμμος is primarily used in the NT in a figurative sense referring to things which cannot be counted. In such contexts, therefore, what is important is the abundance of sand and not its particular occurrence beside the sea. Therefore, in many contexts it is possible to say ‘as numerous as the grains of sand.’ In this way one need not specify the particular location if the meaning of innumerable quantity is fully evident.|In some areas of the world there is little or no sand, and therefore it may be necessary to render sand in ⟦Matthew 7:26|Matthew 7:26⟧ as ‘loose soil’ or ‘unpacked dirt.’

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Land in Contrast With the Sea
s.d: a sandy beach or shore
s.c: ἄμμος evidently involves a particular type of αἰγιαλός (LN 1.63) which is sandy. For languages spoken by persons living along a seacoast, there are usually few if any problems involved in distinguishing various types of land bordering the sea, but for persons living in inland areas, it may be necessary to employ a descriptive phrase such as land along the sea and use such a phrase for various occurrences of different terms.

s.d: young of sheep πρόβατον; often used for ritual sacrifice
s.c: In a number of languages a clear distinction is made between male and female lambs. It is therefore essential in any figurative reference to male persons to employ an appropriate term for lamb. In a number of languages, of course, a lamb is simply referred to as a ‘young sheep’ or ‘child sheep.’|Perhaps the most widespread story about cultural differences in Bible translation is the one which refers to the translation of ‘lamb’ as ‘little seal of God’ in an Eskimo language. However, there is no evidence that this type of rendering was ever used, since in matters of appearance, habitat, and behavior, lambs and little seals have practically nothing in common. Furthermore, Eskimo languages have terms for ‘lamb’ and in some instances, at least, use the expression ‘young, woolly goat,’ since wild goats are well known and wool is well known as an imported product.

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Pay, Price, Cost
s.d: that which is given as a means of recompense or repayment
s.c: One may also translate ‘repayment to their parents and grandparents’ as ‘to pay back to their parents and grandparents for what these have done for them’ or ‘to help their parents and grandparents because of what these have done to help them.’

s.dp: Plants › Plants That Are Not Trees
s.d: creeping plant that develops a woody stem when it matures; Vitis vinifera; grows along the ground until it finds a tree or other object to climb, using tendrils; bears bunches of small round fruit that are sweet and juicy; symbol of blessing, prosperity, and happiness
s.c: A rendering of ἄμπελος as ‘vine’ rather than as ‘grapevine’ in ⟦John 15:1|John 15:1⟧ may cause serious misunderstanding, since it might refer merely to a vine which does not produce fruit. Accordingly, if there is no particular expression for ‘grapevine,’ it may be more satisfactory in ⟦John 15:1|John 15:1⟧ to speak of ‘fruit bush’ or ‘fruit plant.’ A term in ⟦John 15:1|John 15:1⟧ which would indicate only jungle vines would also result in complete misunderstanding of the function of pruning (see LN 43.12), since such jungle vines are never pruned and in fact are only useful when they have been cut down and used for building purposes.|In some languages a grapevine may be referred to as ‘a bush producing grapes,’ and in certain other languages it is called ‘the wine plant.’

s.d: one who takes care of a vineyard

s.dp: Plants › Plants That Are Not Trees
s.d: (derivative of ἄμπελος ‘grapevine’) a field or garden of grapevines, creeping plants that develop a woody stem when they mature; Vitis vinifera; they grow along the ground until they find a tree or other object to climb, using tendrils; they bear bunches of small round fruit that are sweet and juicy; a symbol of blessing, prosperity, and happiness
s.c: In some instances a vineyard may be described as ‘a farm with grapevines’ or ‘a garden for grapes.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person greeted in the Epistle to the Romans
to assist by intervening on behalf of, primarily in terms of defense
to cast a net in order to catch fish
s.c: The net implied in the use of the verb ἀμφιβάλλω was probably a circular net which had small weights on its edge and which could be thrown by a single person.

s.d: a circular net with weights and a draw rope around its edge; used in fishing
s.c: An ἀμφίβληστρον had small weights attached to the outer border, and it was normally thrown in such a manner as to encircle fish. In trying to obtain a satisfactory equivalent expression in another language, it is not necessary to try to duplicate all the details of form. What is important is that such a net was thrown rather than being dragged.

s.d: to put on clothes, implying the clothing being completely around; see also {D:49.5}
to put on clothing to adorn the outward form of something{N:001}
to put on clothes, implying the clothing being completely around; see also {D:49.5}
to put on clothing to adorn the outward form of something{N:002}

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: the capital of southeast Macedonia

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Thoroughfares: Roads, Streets, Paths, etc.
s.d: a thoroughfare within a city
the totality of two
s.c: In a number of languages ἀμφότεροι may be rendered as ‘the two.’

s.d: all of a few (three or more)
s.c: It is clear that in ⟦Acts 19:16|Acts 19:16⟧ ἀμφότεροι must refer to the seven sons of a Jewish high priest named Sceva.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Holy, Pure
s.d: pertaining to not being subject to blame and hence morally irreproachable
s.g: blameless; without blame; being one who cannot be blamed

s.d: a generic term for any kind of spice, though often a specific reference to amomum, an Indian type of spice
s.c: In most translations ἄμωμον is interpreted as spice in general, and though in all languages some types of herb-derivative condiments are employed, there may be no general term for such spices. One may, however, in some instances use a descriptive phrase, for example, ‘good-tasting herbs’ or ‘flavoring leaves.’

s.d: pertaining to having no defect or blemish
s.c: In ⟦1 Peter 1:19|1 Peter 1:19⟧ the overall context is figurative, but the immediate meaning must be regarded as literal.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Holy, Pure
s.d: pertaining to being without fault and hence morally blameless
